coordinate_system.primary_axis: Datum A rotational axis; view-local X in main_view_bottom and view-local Z in section_a_a are treated as the same physical machining axis.
coordinate_system.orientation_notes: The part is treated as an axisymmetric turned component. Section A-A is a longitudinal cut through the rotational axis; the end view shows concentric outer and internal features. Axial access is from the B and C end faces, with radial access for exterior turning operations.
coordinate_system.datum_origin: Datum A axis, with axial location controlled by the B/C end-face datum planes.

datum_scheme.datum_hierarchy_notes: Datum A is the primary rotational datum axis defined from the main external cylinder. Datums B and C are opposing planar end-face datums defined in Section A-A. The GD&T controls reference A for runout-controlled rotational features and C for perpendicularity of the main cylinder axis; no broader datum-reference-frame order beyond the individual controls is explicitly shown.

assumptions.text: View coordinate axes were treated as local to each view; the main_view_bottom longitudinal X-axis and the section_a_a longitudinal Z-axis were interpreted as the same physical rotational axis for datum and face matching.

section_a_a:F1 was grouped with main_view_bottom:F4, and section_a_a:F2 was grouped with main_view_bottom:F5, based on matching left/right end-face descriptions and the Datum C/B definitions. The section_a_a observations were made canonical because they carry the datum evidence.

main_view_bottom:F1 and section_a_a:F3 were not grouped even though both are external cylinders, because their extracted diameter and length values conflict and no direct cross-reference identifies them as the same physical cylindrical surface. They were treated as separate coaxial/datum-related exterior cylindrical features.

main_view_left:F1 was treated as an aggregate end-view observation for the concentric outer and internal features in section_a_a, because it shows the A-A cut passing through the concentric circles but provides no individual dimensions.
isometric_view:F1 was treated as a visual aggregate for the section_a_a outer/body context only; it was not used as canonical because it contains no dimensions.

isometric_view:F2 was assigned only to the section_a_a:F4 left/stepped internal cavity group as the closest matching complex internal cavity observation; it was not propagated to the individually defined central and right bore groups to avoid applying the isometric BLIND condition to features where that condition is not explicitly established.

detail_b:F1 was grouped to section_a_a:F4 based on the explicit SEE DETAIL B cross-reference. section_a_a:F4 was chosen as canonical because Detail B lacks parent axial position; customer confirmation is requested due the apparent feature-description and diameter mismatch.
DETAIL B applies exclusively to parent feature section_a_a:F4 as designated by the SEE DETAIL B cross-reference callout.
The feature profile in DETAIL B is governed by the complete Ø7±0.1 dimension callout. The partially visible callout near the Section A-A outer profile is excluded from drawing requirements.
